Entries.SourceTerm: 兄弟但改往修來，若不改，大有著你處在

Senses.PreferredTarget: Brothers, change your past and cultivate what is to come; if you do not change, there will be plenty to hold against you.
SearchAliases: Zhaozhou on changing the past and future
Senses.Note: Zhaozhou Congshen voices the original line. Jiqi and Wanfeng quote and answer it; neither is presented as its original speaker.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1319.xml). Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings. The source-headed Zhaozhou Congshen tells his assembly to change the past and cultivate what comes, warning of the consequences if they refuse.

Senses.Explanation: Two later teachers challenge the tone and force of Zhaozhou Congshen's old warning. The X68 recorded saying preserves Zhaozhou telling the assembly to change the past and cultivate the future, otherwise there is much for which they may be held to account. Jiqi Hongchu raises the line at a late address, calls Zhaozhou unexpectedly sharp, asks a monk where Zhaozhou himself should be held, and turns the warning back on everyone before leaving the hall. Wanfeng Tongzhen quotes the same line in an old-case discussion and wonders why a teacher usually skilled at sweeping away and building up suddenly sounds so cautious. These are an original hall warning and two different later appraisals.
